SMTO-CFG-0001 — A safety setting has a value SMTO doesn't recognize

GUID: b89e5cfe-9587-48c0-a22d-98b205b27658
Slug: invalid-runtime-policy
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • A safety setting, such as Unsafe actions or an Agent Check, was sent with a name or value SMTO doesn't recognize. SMTO rejected it, so nothing was changed or run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page in your browser, then make the change again using the options shown. A page left open across an SMTO update can send setting names the server no longer uses.
  2. For unsafe actions, open Settings › Security › Security and pick Run blindly, Ask or Disallow under Unsafe actions. Those three choices are the only values SMTO accepts for this setting.
  3. For Agent Checks, open Agent Checks in the message box controls and set each check again from the list shown there. Each check only accepts on or off, and a check missing from the list was renamed or removed.
  4. If a task step failed with this message, open Settings › Setup › Gateways and compare the Gateway's Installed version with Server installed version. If they differ, select Update to once its running tasks finish. A Gateway on a different version may not understand the safety settings sent with each command. Updating restarts the Gateway, which stops anything it is running.

What success looks like

  • The setting saves without an error, or the task step runs on the Gateway.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details in this panel and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't turn off Agent Checks or set Unsafe actions to Run blindly just to make the error go away; that removes safety protections.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A runtime policy value failed strict validation: an unsafe_action_policy outside run_blindly, ask and disallow, an unknown Agent Check ID or non-boolean check value in a prompt or run override, or a Gateway rejecting the Server's forwarded runtime, monitoring, redaction or resource-locking policy (invalid_runtime_policy, executed=false).

What this means

  • A runtime-check ID/value, policy enum, override or forwarded Gateway policy envelope fails its closed field/type/version checks. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • A runtime-check ID/value, policy enum, override or forwarded Gateway policy envelope fails its closed field/type/version checks.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact rejected key, boolean/enum type and Gateway forwarding schema rather than disabling checks to accept it.

How to fix it

  • Find the rejected key in Technical details or the Server or Gateway log: set unsafe_action_policy to run_blindly, ask or disallow, and use only registered Agent Check IDs with true or false values. If a Gateway rejected the forwarded policy, align the Gateway and Server versions (Settings › Setup › Gateways update) rather than disabling checks.
  • Correct the named policy field and accepted type or range; retain safety protections.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended policy validates through its owning settings and forwarding boundary.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
